description: 40 frozen Landing Zone capabilities across design areas A–H. Each criterion has three sub-criteria.

criteria.title: Authoritative organization root
criteria.description: A single declared tenant, organization or management account is the landing-zone root. Production resources do not live in unmanaged side-tenants. The root is inventoryable.
sub_criteria: Is there a single declared tenant, organization or management account that is the landing-zone root?
Can that root be exported as a hierarchy (management groups, OUs or folders) with a named owner?
Are production workloads forbidden from existing outside that root?

criteria.title: Management-plane hygiene
criteria.description: The management, payer or bootstrap plane runs only organization services. Application workloads, data and developer sandboxes are not hosted there.
sub_criteria: Is the management, payer or bootstrap account free of application workloads?
Are only organization-level services (identity, logging, policy, connectivity) deployed there?
Is access to that plane separately controlled and reviewed?

criteria.title: Billing and contract alignment
criteria.description: Commercial construct (EA/MCA, payer, billing account) matches the technical organization. Cost, invoice and account ownership can be named.
sub_criteria: Is the billing account, payer or enrollment mapped to the same organization as the technical hierarchy?
Can every in-scope subscription, account or project be attributed to a billing owner?
Are orphaned billing scopes (unused enrollments, extra payers) identified and closed or explicitly out of scope?

criteria.title: Administrative boundary clarity
criteria.description: Partner, guest, sandbox and merged-company tenants are named. The assessment scope is a declared set of roots, not 'whatever we found'.
sub_criteria: Are partner, guest, sandbox and acquisition tenants explicitly in-scope or out-of-scope?
Is there an inventory of extra directories, organizations or billing accounts?
Does Step 0 lock the in-scope roots before scoring begins?

criteria.title: Root recovery and emergency access
criteria.description: Loss of the cloud-root identity does not mean loss of the estate. Emergency access is designed, stored, tested and monitored — not a password in a ticket.
sub_criteria: Is there a documented emergency-access path to the tenant, management account or org super-admin?
Is that path stored offline or in a vault, with dual control, and tested on a cadence?
Are root/emergency authentications logged and alerted?

criteria.title: Federated workforce identity
criteria.description: Workforce access uses the corporate identity provider. Cloud-local users are not the primary human identity. Joiners, movers and leavers follow the IdP.
sub_criteria: Is workforce sign-in federated from the corporate identity provider to every in-scope cloud?
Are cloud-local human users the exception, inventoried, and expiry-bound?
Does leaver processing in the IdP actually remove cloud access?

criteria.title: Time-bound privileged access
criteria.description: Privileged roles are eligible, activated, time-bound and logged. Standing Global Admin, AdministratorAccess or organizationAdmin for humans is not the operating model.
sub_criteria: Are privileged roles eligible rather than permanently assigned to humans?
Is activation time-bound, approved or justified, and written to an audit log?
Is standing owner-equivalent access on humans treated as an exception with an expiry?

criteria.title: Workload identity without long-lived keys
criteria.description: Compute, pipelines and services authenticate with federated or managed identities. Long-lived access keys and downloaded JSON keys are not the default.
sub_criteria: Do platform and application workloads use managed or federated identities rather than stored keys?
Are remaining long-lived keys inventoried, aged, and on a removal path?
Do CI/CD platforms federate into the cloud rather than store cloud secrets?

criteria.title: Least-privilege inheritance
criteria.description: Role assignment follows the hierarchy. Owner-equivalent at tenant, org or management-group root is rare, named, and not used for daily work.
sub_criteria: Are role assignments scoped to the landing zone or workload, not the organization root, by default?
Is Owner / AdministratorAccess / roles/owner at root limited to a break-glass set?
Can the platform show who has owner-equivalent rights, where, and why?

criteria.title: Monitored break-glass
criteria.description: Emergency access exists, is dual-controlled, is unused in daily operations, and fires a detection when used.
sub_criteria: Do named break-glass identities exist, with dual control, outside normal federation failure modes?
Are they excluded from daily use by policy and culture?
Does use generate a high-severity alert within minutes?

criteria.title: Hierarchy that encodes policy
criteria.description: Management groups, OUs or folders are the policy inheritance spine. Placement of a workload decides its guardrails, not a wiki page.
sub_criteria: Does every in-scope subscription, account or project sit under a designed hierarchy node?
Is policy inherited from those nodes rather than applied one-by-one as a hobby?
Can the platform explain what moving a workload to another node would change?

criteria.title: Platform versus application landing zones
criteria.description: Identity, connectivity, management and security sit in platform landing zones. Applications sit in application landing zones that consume those services.
sub_criteria: Are platform services (identity, hub network, logging, security) separated from application workloads?
Do application landing zones consume shared services rather than rebuild them?
Is ownership of platform vs application landing zones named?

criteria.title: Naming and tagging enforced
criteria.description: A naming and tagging standard exists, is machine-enforced at vending time, and untagged or illegally named resources are visible as exceptions.
sub_criteria: Is there a documented naming and tagging standard for subscriptions, accounts, projects and resources?
Is it enforced at create-time (policy, SCP or vending pipeline), not only in a slide?
Are violations tracked and remediated rather than accepted as noise?

criteria.title: Governed subscription / account / project vending
criteria.description: New isolation units are created by a pipeline or service catalog, with identity, network, policy and logging attached at birth — not by a portal click and a hope.
sub_criteria: Are new subscriptions, accounts or projects created through a vending path rather than ad-hoc portal clicks?
Does the vended unit land in the correct hierarchy node with baseline policy, identity and logging?
Can the platform show the last N vended units and their owners?

criteria.title: Environment separation
criteria.description: Production is a different landing-zone node from non-production. Blast radius, identity and data paths respect that line.
sub_criteria: Are production and non-production in distinct hierarchy nodes or landing zones?
Can non-production identities not administer production by default?
Is data-path isolation (network, identity, key) designed, not accidental?

criteria.title: Hub topology with inspection
criteria.description: A designed hub (hub-spoke, Virtual WAN, Transit Gateway, Shared VPC) exists. Spoke-to-spoke and egress paths are intentional. Inspection is a placement, not a hope.
sub_criteria: Is there a designed hub that spokes must use for shared and egress traffic?
Are inspection points (firewall, IDS, web proxy) placed on those forced paths?
Is spoke-to-spoke traffic an explicit pattern rather than a mesh accident?

criteria.title: Owned hybrid connectivity
criteria.description: ExpressRoute, Direct Connect, Interconnect, VPN and SD-WAN land in the platform, not in an application subscription. Ownership, redundancy and failover are named.
sub_criteria: Do hybrid circuits terminate in a platform connectivity landing zone?
Are redundancy, failover and who-to-call documented and tested?
Can application teams not create competing hybrid paths as a side door?

criteria.title: Central DNS
criteria.description: Private DNS is a platform service. Resolution of on-premises, PaaS private endpoints and landing-zone names is consistent. Split-brain is a tracked exception.
sub_criteria: Is private DNS administered as a platform service rather than per application?
Do private endpoints and hybrid names resolve consistently in every landing zone?
Are rogue DNS forwarders inventoried?

criteria.title: Private-by-default
criteria.description: Public endpoints are denied or exception-gated. PaaS public access is off unless an expiry-bound exemption exists.
sub_criteria: Is public network access denied by policy for relevant services unless exempted?
Are remaining public endpoints inventoried with owner and expiry?
Is internet egress a controlled hub path rather than every NIC for itself?

criteria.title: Segmentation by landing zone
criteria.description: Application landing zones are network segments, not names. Identity and network together define who can talk to whom.
sub_criteria: Does each application landing zone have a defined network segment and peering model?
Are east-west rules explicit (allow-lists), not 'all spokes can talk'?
Is production segmented from non-production on the wire, not only in a naming standard?

criteria.title: Preventive security baseline
criteria.description: A defined security baseline is enforced at the landing zone (policy, SCP, org policy), not offered as a starter template that teams may ignore.
sub_criteria: Is a security baseline assigned to every in-scope landing zone at birth?
Are high-severity misconfigurations denied rather than only reported?
Is the baseline versioned and owned by security + platform together?

criteria.title: Central threat detection
criteria.description: Cloud-native detections (Defender, GuardDuty, SCC) are on at organization scope. Findings land in a SOC path, not in a per-subscription inbox nobody reads.
sub_criteria: Are native threat-detection services enabled at organization or tenant scope?
Do findings route to a named SOC or detection owner with an SLA?
Are silent subscriptions, accounts or projects (detection off) inventoried as exceptions?

criteria.title: Encryption and key management
criteria.description: Data is encrypted with platform-managed or customer-managed keys that the landing zone actually uses. Keys are not in code, and CMK is not a slide.
sub_criteria: Is encryption at rest required by policy for data stores in scope?
If CMK is claimed, are keys in a platform key landing zone with rotation and access logs?
Are plaintext secrets or unencrypted disks treated as findings, not style?

criteria.title: Secrets management
criteria.description: Secrets live in a vault service, are rotated, and are not the identity. Pipeline variables and wikis are not the secret store.
sub_criteria: Is there a mandated secret store for platform and application secrets?
Are secrets rotated, access-logged, and free of long-lived cloud keys used as identity?
Do code, wikis and CI variables still hold production secrets?

criteria.title: Security operations placement
criteria.description: Security tooling has a landing-zone home (audit/security subscription) and a RACI with the SOC. Security is not 'a marketplace product in each app team'.
sub_criteria: Is there a platform security landing zone that hosts org-level security services?
Is the SOC / CSIRT relationship named, including who triages cloud findings?
Are overlapping security tools inventoried rather than silently duplicated?

criteria.title: Central activity and audit logs
criteria.description: Organization activity (Entra, CloudTrail, Cloud Audit Logs) is exported to a platform log landing zone with retention and immutability appropriate to the risk.
sub_criteria: Are tenant, organization or account activity logs exported centrally, not left in each landing zone?
Is retention and immutability defined and met?
Can security and platform query those logs without asking application teams?

criteria.title: Inventory as landing-zone truth
criteria.description: The platform can list isolation units, policy assignments and network paths from APIs this week. Spreadsheets are a cache, not the system of record.
sub_criteria: Can the platform export the current hierarchy, policy assignments and identity bindings on demand?
Is that export used as assessment evidence rather than a slide from last year?
Are unknown isolation units a finding, not a surprise in the workshop?

criteria.title: Baseline monitoring and alerting
criteria.description: Platform health (identity, network, policy, logging pipeline) has monitors. Application APM is welcome; it is not a substitute for platform observability.
sub_criteria: Are there monitors on the logging pipeline, hybrid connectivity, policy compliance and identity health?
Do those alerts reach a platform on-call, not only an application team?
Is 'we have Azure Monitor / CloudWatch / Cloud Monitoring' evidenced for the platform plane, not only for one app?

criteria.title: Platform backup and restore
criteria.description: The landing zone itself — identity config, DNS, policy, IaC state, key material — has a restore story. Application backup does not restore the foundation.
sub_criteria: Is there a restore path for platform configuration (IaC state, DNS, policy, identity)?
Are key-vault / KMS and secret restores tested?
Has a platform restore been rehearsed, not only documented?

criteria.title: Update and agent baseline
criteria.description: Guest OS, agents, and policy deployments that the platform owns have an update path. Snowflake images are exceptions with owners.
sub_criteria: Is there a platform-owned update path for OS, agents or policy guest configuration in scope?
Are unmanaged agents and golden-image drift visible?
Is 'we use Kubernetes so this does not apply' evidenced, not assumed, where relevant?

criteria.title: Policy inheritance from the root
criteria.description: Guardrails are assigned at hierarchy nodes and inherited. Per-subscription policy as a cottage industry is the exception, not the system.
sub_criteria: Are core guardrails assigned at management group, OU or folder — not only on individual isolation units?
Can the platform show effective policy on a given landing zone?
Are conflicting assignments visible and owned?

criteria.title: Deny for insecure defaults
criteria.description: A small, named set of high-blast-radius actions is denied (public data, disable logging, leave the org, user-access-admin). Audit-only is not a deny.
sub_criteria: Is there a named deny set for high-blast-radius misconfigurations?
Are those denies in force on production landing zones, not only in a sandbox?
Is audit-only clearly labelled as detection, not prevention?

criteria.title: Exemptions with owner and expiry
criteria.description: Every exemption has a named owner, a reason, an expiry and a review. Permanent 'exclude this MG' is itself a finding.
sub_criteria: Are policy exemptions recorded with owner, reason and expiry?
Is there a review cadence that actually retires them?
Are root-level exclusions treated as landing-zone risk, not housekeeping?

criteria.title: Cost and tag guardrails
criteria.description: The landing zone enforces the commercial minimum: required tags, allowed regions, maybe budgets. FinOps is a consumer of this; it is not a substitute for it.
sub_criteria: Are required tags or labels enforced at vending or by policy?
Are allowed regions constrained?
Are budgets or cost-anomaly signals attached to landing zones with owners?

criteria.title: Compliance evidence export
criteria.description: Compliance is a query (policy compliance, Config, SCC posture), not a screenshot of a dashboard from last quarter.
sub_criteria: Can the platform export current compliance against the assigned baseline?
Is that export used as assessment evidence?
Are non-compliant resources owned, not only counted?

criteria.title: Platform as code
criteria.description: Hierarchy, policy, identity grants, hub network and logging sinks are in versioned IaC with review. The portal is for break-glass, not for the weekly change.
sub_criteria: Are the platform landing zones defined in versioned IaC (Terraform, Bicep, CDK, Pulumi, Config Connector)?
Do reviews and promotions follow a pipeline, not a shared admin login?
Is portal change of platform resources treated as drift?

criteria.title: Vending pipeline
criteria.description: A request becomes a landing zone with identity, network, policy and logging already on. Human time is approval, not clicking 40 blades.
sub_criteria: Is there a pipeline or catalog item that vends a subscription, account or project into the right node?
Does the vended unit boot with the baseline attached?
Is the request-to-ready time measured?

criteria.title: Drift detection
criteria.description: The platform notices when reality leaves the code. Drift is a ticket with an owner, not a shrug.
sub_criteria: Is there a drift signal on platform IaC or on policy/config?
Does drift create a reviewable event rather than a silent overwrite?
Are recurring ClickOps offenders visible?

criteria.title: Guardrailed self-service
criteria.description: Application teams can get a landing zone or a spoke without a platform engineer performing the ritual. Guardrails do the saying-no.
sub_criteria: Can an application team request a compliant landing zone without a platform engineer clicking it into existence?
Are denied requests explained by policy, not by personality?
Is self-service actually used, or is it a demo?

criteria.title: Platform change management
criteria.description: Changes to identity, hub, policy and logging have a path, a reviewer, and a way to stop a bad change. Hotfixes are logged as such.
sub_criteria: Is there a defined change path for the platform landing zones?
Are emergency hotfixes recorded and followed by code catch-up?
Can a bad policy assignment be rolled back from code, not from memory?
